mutations.reason: Drops the claim that a template leaves `rsp` as it was. Every template still leaves `rsp` unchanged, so no theorem becomes false for the mutant; but the control-flow refinement (`cfspec::cf_refines`) states `preserved_r`, which includes `rsp`, and `cfop::lemma_preserved_to_r` derives it from `preserved`, so that derivation no longer goes through. Only a proof step breaks: not coverage. A certified kill needs a theorem the mutant falsifies, which `rsp` preservation by the code between exits (the confinement theorem, jit.md exit criterion 2) will give once the back end is tied to it.

The A64 template for a signed less-than comparison would give `cset` the condition `lt` (11) instead of its inverse `ge` (10) (a `cset` is `csinc` on the inverse of the condition that sets the result), so it would return 0 where LIR's `lt_s` is 1: after `cmp 1, 2` the `N` and `V` flags differ, so `lt` holds. `flags::lemma_cc_icmp_blank32` is false for the mutant at `lt_s`, 32 bits, 1 and 2.

The A64 template for `eq` would give `cset` the condition `eq` (0) instead of its inverse `ne` (1), so it would return 0 where LIR's `eq` is 1: after `cmp 1, 1` the `Z` flag is set. `flags::lemma_cc_icmp_blank32` is false for the mutant at `eq`, 32 bits, 1 and 1.

The A64 template for an unsigned less-than comparison would give `cset` the condition `lo` (3) instead of its inverse `hs` (2), so it would return 0 where LIR's `lt_u` is 1: after `cmp 1, 2` the carry is clear, so `lo` holds. `flags::lemma_cc_icmp_blank32` is false for the mutant at `lt_u`, 32 bits, 1 and 2.

The A64 template for an unsigned greater-than comparison would give `cset` the condition `hi` (8) instead of its inverse `ls` (9), so it would return 0 where LIR's `gt_u` is 1: after `cmp 2, 1` the carry is set and `Z` clear, so `hi` holds. `flags::lemma_cc_icmp_blank32` is false for the mutant at `gt_u`, 32 bits, 2 and 1.

The second 16-bit chunk of a constant (the `movk ..., lsl #16` immediate) would be taken from bit 17 instead of bit 16, so the four chunks no longer add up to the word: for 0x10000 the chunks would all be 0. `bitmid::lemma_chunks` is false for the mutant at 0x10000.

The `movz` of the `f64.neg` template would load 2^62 instead of the sign bit 2^63 into `x1`, so `eor` would flip the wrong bit. `bitmid::lemma_neg_template_mask` (which `lemma_mid_neg` rests on) is false for the mutant.
